`\rowcolor` is a LaTeX command used to color entire rows in tables. It's part of the `colortbl` package (which also requires the `xcolor` or `color` package).

## Basic Usage

```latex
\usepackage{colortbl}  % or \usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\begin{tabular}{cc}
\rowcolor{gray!30}
Header 1 & Header 2 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 \\
\rowcolor{blue!20}
Data 3 & Data 4 \\
\end{tabular}
```

## Syntax

```latex
\rowcolor{color}[left overhang][right overhang]
```

- **color**: The color name or specification
- **left/right overhang**: Optional parameters to extend coloring beyond cell borders

## Common Examples

### 1. **Alternating Row Colors**
```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\rowcolor{gray!50}
Name & Age & City \\
\hline
John & 25 & NYC \\
\rowcolor{gray!20}
Jane & 30 & LA \\
Mike & 28 & Chicago \\
\rowcolor{gray!20}
Lisa & 35 & Boston \\
\end{tabular}
```

### 2. **Using Named Colors**
```latex
\rowcolor{red}      % Full red
\rowcolor{blue!30}  % 30% blue
\rowcolor{green!50!yellow}  % Mix of green and yellow
```

### 3. **Automatic Alternating Rows**
```latex
\rowcolors{2}{gray!25}{white}  % Starting from row 2, alternate colors
\begin{tabular}{cc}
Header 1 & Header 2 \\
\hline
Row 1 & Data \\
Row 2 & Data \\
Row 3 & Data \\
\end{tabular}
```

## Important Notes

- Place `\rowcolor` at the **beginning** of the row (right after `\\` or at table start)
- Conflicts may occur with vertical lines - consider using `booktabs` instead
- For header rows, combine with `\textbf{}` for emphasis
